propositions: Per-pair overlap judgment issues 2N calls (one per candidate per ordering); batching candidates into labeled lists reduces this to 2*ceil(N/batch) calls, eliminating N-1 redundant system prompt transmissions per ordering.

Hoisting the query digest into the system prompt (ticket 8415) reached 873 tokens but fell short of the 1024-token caching floor; adding batch protocol instructions to the system block lifts the prefix to 1337 tokens, clearing the floor and enabling prefix caching.

Batching increases precision risk through cross-candidate contamination (shared artifacts or verdict drift); this risk must be measured and reported, not asserted, using controlled before/after runs and a synthetic positive-control candidate.

The batching change reduces total input tokens from 18,494 (8415 single-pair) to 9,116 (batched) on the same corpus—a 49.3% reduction—with cache writes of 1,331 tokens on the first of two calls and cache reads on the second, versus zero cache activity in the prior build.
